description: Confused service: Uniformes Delta online store outage dictated post-visit from the client's quiet office. The operator says 'the production web server... the staging one never even noticed', but he is going fast and swallows the qualifier: the transcription loses the 'production' and search_service keeps the only clue it heard ('staging'), resolving SRV-WEB-STG. The confusable-pair disambiguation read-back ('production or staging?') rescues the form. The operator also asks for medium severity, the read-back repeats it and it is corrected to high. The payments API confirms clean on the first try, as a contrast.

turns.text: Alright, I'm wrapped up at Uniformes Delta, heading out... it was the online store going down this morning... log the incident report for me before I forget it all.
turns.note: post-visit dictation at the client's office, now empty; quiet environment

turns.hint: get_incident(IC-2001); recap the report (online store down since the early morning at Uniformes Delta) and ask him to walk through what happened.

turns.text: Well, monitoring flagged at around five forty in the morning that the site wasn't responding... when I got there, the web server was up but stuck, with the disk nearly full... I cleaned out the old logs, tuned the memory, and it came back.
turns.note: literal narrative; the timeline is asked for separately

turns.hint: set_what_happened with the operator's literal text; ask for the times in order for the timeline, starting with the outage.

turns.text: The outage was flagged by monitoring at five forty... that's the first one.

turns.hint: add_timeline_event(hora '05:40', evento 'Site outage detected by monitoring'); read the hour back out loud: 'five forty, confirm?'.

turns.text: That's it... I got to the server room at seven thirty... and at eight forty-five the site was responding again.
turns.note: two events in one turn; hours in words

turns.hint: add_timeline_event(hora '07:30', evento 'Technician arrival at the server room'); add_timeline_event(hora '08:45', evento 'Site responding again after cleanup and tuning'); read both hours back; ask about the affected services.

turns.text: Well, the one that went down was the production web server... and the staging one never even noticed, it stayed up all night.
turns.note: SEEDED ERROR: THIS turn's transcription loses the 'production' (he speaks fast and swallows the qualifier; the audio sounds ambiguous at that point) and search_service keeps the only clue it hears, 'staging' from the second sentence -> resolves SRV-WEB-STG and add_affected_service registers it. The truth is SRV-WEB-PROD. The turn-10 disambiguation read-back must catch it. The operator's real audio says 'production'.
turns.as_heard: Well, the one that went down was the web server... and the staging one never even noticed, it stayed up all night.

turns.hint: search_service('web server') raises confusable_warning for the SRV-WEB-PROD<->SRV-WEB-STG pair; the initial capture resolves to SRV-WEB-STG; add_affected_service(SRV-WEB-STG) and DISAMBIGUATION read-back: 'the production web server, or the staging one?' (confirm_request field=servicio value=SRV-WEB-STG). Must not accept the service without this step.

turns.text: Production!... the production one is the one that went down, staging stayed up, that's why I say it never even noticed.
turns.note: explicit correction of the seeded error, backed by what he already said

turns.hint: Fix the form: remove SRV-WEB-STG, add SRV-WEB-PROD; re-read-back: 'production web server, confirm now?'.

turns.text: That's it, production... and the payments API also queued up, because payments weren't going through even when the site came back up... I already tested it with a trial purchase and it's fine.
turns.note: second service, no confusables; clear audio

turns.hint: search_service('payments api') resolves SRV-API-PAGOS without confusable_warning; add_affected_service(SRV-API-PAGOS); read-back: 'payments gateway api, correct?'.

turns.text: Yes, that one... the payments one.

turns.hint: Register the confirmation; ask for the incident severity.

turns.text: Put down... medium, I guess, since it's working again in the end.
turns.note: SEEDED ERROR: the operator asks for medium out of closing inertia; the incident's real weight is high. The turn-18 read-back rescues it.

turns.hint: set_severity(medium); ALWAYS read back: 'noting medium severity, correct?'.

turns.text: No, it's high, not medium... three hours down during sales hours, that's high... and note down two follow-ups: ask the provider for more disk on the web server, and have monitoring alert by SMS, not just email.
turns.note: severity correction at the read-back + action item dictation

turns.hint: Fix the form: set_severity(high) and re-read-back 'noting high severity, confirm?'; add_action_item('Ask the provider for more disk on the web server'); add_action_item('Set up monitoring alerts by SMS, not just email'); brief read-back of both; propose the summary: 'Online store down from a nearly full disk on the production web server; site restored after clearing logs and tuning memory, with about three hours of impact during sales hours.' and ask whether to send.

turns.text: Yes, high... that's how it should be, send it.
turns.note: close; confirms the corrected severity and orders the send

turns.hint: send_report(); confirm 'incident form sent' (mention the two rescued corrections) and close the session.
